description: Runs a Playwright test in the Statuser sandbox exactly like a scheduled scenario run, without creating or changing a monitor: no point on the graph, no incident. Use it to check a script before `monitor_create`/`monitor_update`. Waits for the run to finish — up to `request_timeout` plus browser start-up — and returns the verdict (`passed`, `failed`, `timed_out`, or `runner_error` when the sandbox could not run it; that one does not count towards the limit), the failed test, the Playwright error, the console output, and screenshot, video and trace links that work for an hour. Requires `scenarios_limit` above zero on the current plan. One on-demand run per account at a time and at most 30 test runs in 10 minutes (409 and 429 otherwise).

confirm.description: Set to true to authorize this write/destructive call even if STATUSER_ALLOW_WRITE is not enabled in the server config. Required for one-off overrides.

location.description: Where the run goes from. Default `msk-1`. Use the location the monitor will run from: the address the site sees is often what the scenario checks.

request_timeout.description: Limit for the whole run in seconds, no more than `scenario_max_timeout_seconds` of the plan. Default 30.

scenario_env.description: Environment variables of the run, read in the test as `process.env.NAME`. With `server_id` they go on top of the stored ones: a string sets a variable, `null` drops it for this run.

scenario_script.description: Playwright test, one file, using `test` and `expect` from `@playwright/test` — the same rules as `scenario_script` of `monitor_create`.

server_id.description: A saved `scenario` monitor whose environment variables are used for the run — so stored passwords need not be passed again.

name: scenario_test
title: Test a scenario without saving
